title: A written retrospective: what you would do differently

videos.script: A project is finished when it meets lesson 2's definition, not when it is perfect. The last thing it needs is a page that says so: what went well, what did not, and what you would do differently. {{finished}} That page is a retrospective, and for a portfolio it is worth more than it looks. It answers the interview's last question before it is asked, and it is the only document in the repository about you rather than the code. {{worth}} This lesson gathers the evidence from loanbook's history, writes its retrospective in full, and says where the page lives. Then the course ends, and the next one, first-job, takes the finished project to the people who will read it.
